I have been farming these 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. I am 70 now, finished middle school. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan, so they send some money home, but this land is still what feeds us. Six people in the house means I cannot afford a bad year.

For the winter wheat, I will plant Jimai 22. I have used it for three years now. My neighbor Lao Zhang switched to it and got over 1000 jin per mu last year, so I will keep it. I buy 15 kg of seed per mu. Before sowing in October, I do rotary tillage to break up the soil. For fertilizer, I put down 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind from the dealer — and then at jointing in March I spread another 25 kg per mu of urea. That gives me about 18 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: once after sowing, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray four times — herbicide once after the wheat comes up, insecticide twice when the aphids come, and fungicide once at heading. I expect 500 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

For the summer maize, I plant Denghai 605 hybrid seed. I learned from the dealer that this one resists lodging. I sow 2.5 kg per mu right after wheat harvest in early June — no time to waste, and I do no-tillage, just plant into the wheat stubble like everyone else around here. At sowing I put 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer, and when the plants are at the big trumpet stage I add 20 kg per mu of urea. That is about 12 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice — once at jointing and once at silking if the rain does not come. I spray three times: herbicide with the planting, and insecticide twice because the corn borer is bad some years. I expect 550 kg per mu.

I thought about cutting back on fertilizer because the price went up, but last year I used a little less urea on the maize and my yield was 50 jin lower per mu than my cousin's. That taught me a lesson. Better to spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I watch what the neighbors do, and most people on this lane use about the same amounts. I will do the same.
